saints.name: St. John XXIII
saints.title: Pope
saints.shortBlurb: The “Good Pope” of peasant stock who, in a brief pontificate, summoned the Second Vatican Council…
biography: Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli was born on 25 November 1881 at Sotto il Monte near Bergamo, the son of peasant sharecroppers. Ordained priest in 1904, he served as secretary to the bishop of Bergamo and as a military chaplain through the First World War.

Made a bishop in 1925, he spent nearly twenty years as a papal representative in Bulgaria, Turkey, and Greece, labouring in the Second World War to rescue Jews from deportation. As nuncio to France from 1944 he steered the French Church through the Liberation, and in 1953 was created cardinal and named Patriarch of Venice.

Elected pope on 28 October 1958 at the age of seventy-six and thought a caretaker, he stunned the Church within three months by announcing an ecumenical council. In a pontificate of under five years he issued the encyclicals Mater et Magistra and Pacem in Terris and visited Rome's hospitals and prisons like a parish priest.

He died of stomach cancer on 3 June 1963, mourned across the world as 'Good Pope John'. Beatified in 2000 and canonized by Pope Francis in 2014, his memorial is kept on 11 October, the anniversary of the Council's opening.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. John XXIII (vatican.va)
